summary: Dynamic prewarm backpressure triggers tenant unpin and cross-variant reroute during sparse canary window
description:
Issue summary: Several requests from BrightForms experienced sudden model unpinning and were routed to a degraded variant during a scheduled sparse canary that uses on-demand prewarm probes. Impact: A subset of tenant traffic (~3-6% of their requests during the window) saw higher-latency and quality regressions as requests hit a quantized fallback variant; no data leak observed. This appears tightly correlated with backpressure on the dynamic prewarm probe subsystem when prewarm worker pods were transiently CPU-starved.

Observed behaviour: During a low-traffic canary slice (~5% target) running an on-demand prewarm strategy, the orchestrator marked some cohorts as unhealthy because prewarm health probes timed out under backpressure. That path triggers an unpin and fallback routing to a degraded variant. Expected behaviour: Prewarm timeouts should be isolated to prewarm probe metrics and should not trigger immediate unpinning of tenant pins for slices below the configured threshold; routing should honor explicit version pins during canary windows.

Impact severity: Customer reports higher error-rate and lower-quality responses for targeted endpoints used in their live beta tests. Financial impact low but product impact medium for BrightForms.

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket differs from typical prewarm/unpin incidents because it reproduces under sparse canary slice + on-demand prewarm load pattern rather than during full-rollout autoscale events.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a sparse canary (5% weight) with on-demand prewarm enabled on dedicated capacity in us-east.
2) Deploy a new quantized model variant that has a heavier prewarm kernel initialization (simulated by heavy CPU work in prewarm hook).
3) Simulate noisy neighbor CPU pressure on prewarm workers by running a short CPU burner during prewarm window.
4) Send steady low QPS traffic from a single tenant session and observe orchestrator health events and routing decisions.
5) Observe pin change events in control-plane audit logs and routing outcomes at the edge.

Expected: Prewarm failures should not flip tenant pins; orchestrator should deprioritize prewarm but keep pinned routing.
Actual: Prewarm timeouts cause cohort health flip and immediate unpin, resulting in reroute to degraded variant.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: prewarm probe timeouts cascade into the cohort health logic which emits unpin actions; edge-proxy honors unpin immediately. Investigated metrics: prewarm probe latency, prewarm worker CPU steal, orchestrator cohort health transitions, pin-change audit timeline. Found tight correlation between short CPU pressure bursts on prewarm sidecars and immediate unpin audit entries. Edge retry logic also accelerates the routing change by merging two flows: the first timed-out probe triggers an unhealthy mark while concurrent edge retries clear cached pinned routing causing the control-plane to treat the cohort as unpinned. Reviewed orchestration code path in route-orch commit 83a7f3 which contains a prewarm -> cohort-health hook; that hook does an unconditional unhealthy->evict action when probe_count exceeds threshold (no guard for 'sparse' canary slices).

Reproduced in staging: yes (staging dedicated sim node). Repro rate: ~80% with injected CPU burner at prewarm time.

Suspected root cause: cohort-health hook treats on-demand prewarm timeouts the same as persistent health failures and does not check slice weight or recent prewarm backlog. Edge and control-plane race amplifies the window where pin persists on edge but control-plane marks it unpinned; concurrent requests observe mixed routing.
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-11 20:30 UTC): patched orchestrator config to ignore prewarm probe failures for canary slices <= 10% for 5 minutes after canary start (config flag canary.prewarm_tolerance). Rolled config to us-east control-plane only. Advised BrightForms to disable on-demand prewarm on immediate upcoming canary until patch validated.

Long-term plan: engineering ticket to change cohort-health hook to include slice-weight-aware logic and backpressure-resilient prewarm probe handling, add a prewarm backlog metric that gates evictions, and add a control-plane->edge grace window to avoid immediate unpinning until clinical consensus reached. PR planned: github.com/redwood-inference/route-orch/pull/2419 (author: diego-r).

Follow-ups: run a targeted canary with injected CPU variance to validate guardrails, update runbook and add dashboard alert for prewarm_worker_cpu_throttle correlated with pin_eviction events.
